speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether feedback from patients and their families is taken into consideration in a nurse’s performance grading; (b) if so, what is the weightage given to such feedback in a nurse’s performance grading; and (c) how are nurses protected against unfair feedback or abuse by patients or visitors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In general, feedback from patients and their family members is considered an integral part of quality and care improvement for our public healthcare institutions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Positive feedback is conveyed to the nurses and care team to recognise their efforts as well as to encourage and motivate them to keep up the good work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: On the other hand, negative feedback is looked into in case there is a need to address any gaps in quality of care in the spirit of continuous improvement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: These will be looked into fairly, as it is crucial to protect and support staff against abusive patients or family members accompanying patients.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think she mentioned that it is not considered directly in the appraisal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, could I just ask and confirm again that the negative feedback about nurses that they receive from the patient or the family will not directly affect their bonus, appraisal or their promotion as well?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, I think MOH has shared that the Care Ambassador position will be made permanent and there might be some job redesign as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I just ask for a timeframe for that?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is because I think that will help in terms of having some staff members on the ground who are customer service trained in the wards and can handle some of these complaints and feedback that the nurses receive.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I just want to, firstly, mention that the nurses are in the business of patient care.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, it is about making sure that they are taking care of the patients well.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And if there is feedback from the patients and family members, we do have to consider this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is an integral part of the quality and care improvement for public health institutions (PHIs).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But this is something we look at in general.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We do take the concerns of patients and family members and, if it impacts their work and their performance, we then need to take action.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In some ways, it does have some relevance, if it is investigated and if there are some areas where the nurses can improve, this needs to be taken into account.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On the second issue about Care Ambassadors, I note that the Member has been concerned about the workload and having to balance some of the issues that the nurses have raised.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have been working on this, as the Member is aware.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The public healthcare institutions, especially different clusters, all have different efforts that they are putting in place.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Some of these things we are harmonising to see how we can make sure that all the clusters can also step up and have similar practices amongst them.
